guided.note: Issue #64's guided-discovery axis, from TestGuidedSweepAgainstFloci (go test -run TestGuidedSweepAgainstFloci, TF_FLOCI_TEST=1). cold_calls is the estate-wide sweep's API call count over sweep_types with Request.Guided false; guided_routine_calls is the same sweep with Request.Guided true and a fresh snapshot hint (aws_sns_topic present, aws_kms_key and aws_route53_zone absent); guided_verify_calls adds Request.GuidedVerify, which must match cold_calls exactly. The config-driven scan costs nothing in any of the three numbers -- aws_s3_bucket is client-named and never reaches Discover's list/bind machinery, see assertBucketsCostNothing -- so every call counted here belongs to the sweep alone. This is not a ratchet: TestGuidedSweepAgainstFloci's own assertions (guided_routine_calls < cold_calls, guided_verify_calls == cold_calls) are the gate; this section only keeps the artifact's numbers current with the most recent measurement.

note: Issue #64's committed call-count budget. Generated by internal/live/discovery.TestPlanCallBudgetAgainstFloci (go test -run TestPlanCallBudgetAgainstFloci, TF_FLOCI_TEST=1), which reads this file back and fails if a fresh measurement at the same n exceeds calls_total by more than tolerance. calls_total covers discovery.Discover plus projection.BuildFrom for an N=200 aws_s3_bucket estate (tools/estate-gen -count 200) with no prior state - the read cost live-plan pays end to end, not just the discovery/list half. wall_clock_bucket and measured_at are informational only, never gated: floci's performance on whatever machine runs the test, not this repository's code, is what a wall-clock assertion would actually be grading. calls_by_api's per-bucket shape (~17 calls/instance: 3 HEAD /{bucket} plus one GET per S3 subresource the aws_s3_bucket Read covers - acl, cors, encryption, lifecycle, logging, object-lock, policy, replication, requestPayment, versioning, website, accelerate - plus 2 more folded into 'GET /{bucket}/...', which is this proxy's catch-all for any deeper-path or S3-Control-routed call such as bucket tags) is a property of the AWS provider's own aws_s3_bucket Read, not of anything this fork adds; it is recorded here as the baseline this ratchet protects, not as a target to optimize down. This artifact's second measurement (2026-08-13, merging issue #60's parent-read sweep on top of issue #64's own baseline) adds four new per-bucket GETs the first measurement did not pay: encryption, lifecycle, policy and versioning each double from one GET (the aws_s3_bucket Read's own subresource fetch) to two (a second, independent list of the matching aws_s3_bucket_server_side_encryption_configuration / aws_s3_bucket_lifecycle_configuration / aws_s3_bucket_policy / aws_s3_bucket_versioning parent-read child), and publicAccessBlock appears for the first time at one per bucket (aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block has no Read-time analog on aws_s3_bucket itself, only the parent-read child) — the same untaggable-child-via-parent-read discovery issue #60 adds, at the O(N) cost the leg is supposed to pay once the accidental O(N^2) an initial merge of that leg carried (internal/live/discovery/parent_read.go's per-parent unscoped-list loop, fixed the same day) is corrected. See internal/live/discovery/scale_bench_test.go's doc comment for the full method, and internal/live/cloudcontrol/doc.go's 'Retries' section for the backoff policy issue #64 asked for.
